span.label: Is the behaviour of idioms an idiosyncratic property of each idiom, or a consequence of more general constraints?
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Replaces decomposability with an alternative categorization that cross-classifies idioms on two dimensions, figuration and transparency.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: critique

span.label: corpus study
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the idiom whose common characterization is rigidity is searched for in a twenty-billion-word corpus, chosen because the earlier corpora were too small to distinguish an idiom that cannot vary from one that is simply too rare for its variants to appear
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: idioms are cross-classified on two dimensions at once - figuration, whether a literal meaning can be pictured, and transparency, whether the route from that picture to the idiomatic meaning can be recovered - in place of the single decomposable/non-decomposable cut
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: queries are written in a corpus query language over morphological features - part of speech, lemma, clitic - combined with logical operators, which the authors call particularly important for casting a wide net over non-canonical word orders, discontinuous elements and morphological inflections
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: a query wide enough to catch variants also returns results that are not instances of the idiom, so each result is inspected by hand to remove the false positives
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the endpoint is switched from frequency to existence: rather than how often each variation occurs, the study verifies that every type of variation occurs at least once for each idiom
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: argument-structure variation is observable in Hebrew because it is carried by combining one consonantal root with different morphological templates
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the modifier question is split in two: modifications of all types count as variations, while it is the modifier's semantic SCOPE that can provide evidence about whether idiom parts are assigned individual idiomatic meanings
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The study reports no quantitative distribution, because the wide-net queries return false positives that only manual inspection can remove.
span.note: what this limits: any rate or distribution of canonical versus variant forms from this study: the authors state they do not present quantitative data, and why
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The generalisation rests on a limited set of Hebrew verbal idioms.
span.note: what this limits: cross-linguistic or general claims about idiom flexibility: the authors bound the generalisation to a limited set of Hebrew verbal idioms
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The criterion under critique is described as impressionistic and circular: flexibility is taken as evidence for the very property meant to predict it.
span.note: what this limits: decomposability as an independent predictor of flexibility: the paper states the diagnosis is prone to circularity with the behaviour it predicts
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The originating proposal supplied neither precise definitions of its two categories nor a procedure for telling them apart.
span.note: what this limits: the decomposable/non-decomposable split as an operationalised classification: no definitions or decision procedure were given with it
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: An independent corpus study classifying by paraphrase reported the boundary between the two categories as fuzzy.
span.note: what this limits: the decomposable/non-decomposable assignment as sharp: the study that applied it reports the boundary as fuzzy
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Two psycholinguistic studies of the same construct disagree on whether speakers can apply it reliably.
span.note: about this quote: Q-603, 2026-08-16: A RUNNING HEAD IS SPLICED INTO THE MIDDLE OF THIS QUOTE. The staged extraction of this book chapter interleaves its page furniture - '38 2 Verbal multiword expressions: Idiomaticity and flexibility' - into the body text, and this span crosses one occurrence. The quote is an exact substring of the staged file and is NOT a sentence of the paper: the words on either side of the head were never continuous. Read the span with the head deleted. Detected by TOOLS/audit_span_crosses_running_head.py, which finds furniture by repetition rather than by shape; the two shape-based finders (Q-520 all-caps, Q-600 caption) see neither of this chapter's 35 insertions. · what this limits: speaker agreement as established for decomposability: one study found 75% agreement on most items, another classified only 40% of 171 idioms at that threshold
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The rigidity of the field's standard example is shown to depend on corpus size; variation appears only in a very large corpus.
span.note: what this limits: the canonical rigidity of kick the bucket: variation is attestable only in very large corpora, so earlier rigid classifications may reflect corpus size
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The authors' own prediction about cranberry idioms was not borne out, and they say so.
span.note: what this limits: the transparency/figuration hypothesis as confirmed throughout: the cranberry class behaved opposite to the authors' stated expectation
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Neither proposed dimension accounts for idiom behaviour on its own; the paper attributes the effect to an interaction.
span.note: what this limits: transparency or figuration singly as a predictor of flexibility: the paper states neither alone accounts for the behaviour
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the rigidity claim was re-checked against a much larger corpus, enTenTen13
span.note: eliminates: that the idiom looks rigid only because it is RARE - that its apparent fixedness is an artefact of low frequency in a small corpus
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: critiques → Nunberg et al. (1994)
span.note: differs in: WHICH PROPERTY DETERMINES FLEXIBILITY, AND THE CHALLENGE IS MOUNTED ON TWO SEPARATE GROUNDS THE PAPER NUMBERS ITSELF: 'Quotation withheld, and SECOND, in light of empirical investigations in English and in other languages that revealed FLEXIBILITY WITHIN IDIOMS PREVIOUSLY CLASSIFIED AS NON-DECOMPOSABLE.' One ground is about the criterion being unusable, the other about it being wrong where it is usable - and the replacement offered is a pair of graded dimensions, transparency and figuration, rather than a sharper version of the same binary
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: critiques → Nunberg et al. (1994)
span.note: differs in: WHETHER THE CRITERION CAN BE APPLIED INDEPENDENTLY OF WHAT IT PREDICTS. 'determining whether an idiom is decomposable or not is rather IMPRESSIONISTIC, and is PRONE TO CIRCULARITY, WHERE Quotation withheld' - so the property that is supposed to PREDICT flexibility is in practice read OFF flexibility
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: critiques → Nunberg et al. (1994)
span.note: differs in: WHICH WAY THE IMPLICATION RUNS. Decomposability was proposed as 'the semantic property of idioms which PREDICTS their behavior', but 'at times THIS HYPOTHESIS IS TURNED AROUND and idiom flexibility is used as A DEFINING PROPERTY of non-decomposable idioms' - the predictor becomes the definition, at which point the hypothesis cannot fail
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.note: differs in: WHETHER A FUZZY BOUNDARY BLOCKS A CLEAR RESULT. Riehemann classified idioms by whether a similarly structured paraphrase could be found, 'NEVERTHELESS, Quotation withheld. This notwithstanding, her findings show a CLEAR DISTINCTION' - canonical forms accounting for about 75% of occurrences of decomposable idioms against 97% of non-decomposable ones. A classification its own author calls fuzzy still separates the data

span.label: The hypothesis is directional and therefore testable: more transparent and more figurative idioms should bend more.
span.note: retracted: RE-GROUNDED. The published string was in NEITHER copy of the paper. and the difference is TYPOGRAPHY, not wording: ours carried a line-break hyphen (`an id- iom`) and curly quotation marks where the staged body has straight ones. The hyphen is closed by the reader's own check; the quote marks are not, and either alone makes a correct quote unverifiable. The paper states this hypothesis TWICE, verbatim, so the span was extended backwards to the sentence that makes the abstract's occurrence unique.
